name: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier Solo Head, 3 channel
description: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier 3-channel Solo Head as drawn on the 'Preliminary Schematic' set (RECBPR1/2/3, RECBPWR, RECBSUPP, RECBSW1/2 .501): V1a, the CH1 Fender-style stack with Cln/Pushed (RY5/RY5'), shared V2a with the CH1 J175 grid-stopper bypass, CH1 V1b recovery and presence, the CH2/CH3 V2b cold clipper, V3a and V3b cathode follower into each channel's stack, presence and master, the Raw/Vintage/Modern relays RY6-RY9 and the Modern feedback relay RY7, the 4744 master-bus clamp, the series/parallel FX loop (V4a send follower, Mix, V4b, Output, Solo), the LTP PI, four 6L6 (folded in pairs), the tapped OT with 8 ohm feedback, an 8 ohm 4x12-class cab, and the 5U4 x2 / silicon switchable HT supply with Bold/Spongy.

sources.title: Mesa/Boogie 3ch Solo Head 'Preliminary Schematic' (11 pages: front/rear part tables, block diagram RECBBLK.S01, power supplies RECBSUPP.501 with XFMR #561140, preamp RECBPR1/2/3.501, CH2 CH3 voicing RECBSW2.501, switching RECBSW1.501, power amp RECBPWR.501)
sources.note: PRIMARY and the only source for the 3-channel preamp and switching (single source for CH1 and the relay matrix). Pages 4, 6-8, 11 at 377 ppi, pages 5, 9, 10 at 158-162 ppi (CCITT); every value read from 1:1 crops (coordinates in the notes). Handwritten annotations on pp. 7, 9, 10 are a later tracer's and are disclosed where they disagree with the printed circuit.

sources.title: MESA-BOOGIE DUAL RECTIFIER (2-channel, preamp RF-1F = Rev F, '6-93 GEO. M.'), 6 pages incl. power amp, supplies, FX loop and the LDR switching matrix
sources.note: Cross-check for the shared circuitry (PI, power amp, HV supply topology, V2b/V3a/V3b chain, CH2/CH3-style stacks). A different revision: every disagreement is disclosed in the notes, not treated as an error.

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS = 1.5 x the 133.9 V peak at the speaker (8 ohm tap) with Vintage and every catalogue knob dimed (1.0 V, 220 Hz, 192 kHz; the peaks are OT flyback as the 6L6s cut off). Modern dimed 116 V, Raw 106 V, Clean 60 V. Defaults (Raw, knobs 0.5, Output 0.5) at 0.1 V in: 51 V peak.

5U4GB_X2.note: Two 5U4GB plates in parallel: the library 5U4GB perveance (9.4e-4, 44 V at 275 mA, RCA) doubled

controls.label: Gain
controls.note: Ganged to the three channels' GAIN pots (CH1 1MA, CH2 and CH3 250KA): the Mode selector picks which one is in circuit, so the knob always acts on the selected channel

controls.label: Master
controls.note: The three channel MSTR pots (1MA each), ganged as Gain

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: CH1 250KA, CH2 / CH3 1MA, ganged

controls.label: Mid
controls.note: CH1 25KA rheostat, CH2 / CH3 25KL, ganged

controls.label: Treble
controls.note: CH1 250KA, CH2 / CH3 250KL, ganged

controls.label: Presence
controls.note: CH1 250KL treble-shunt rheostat before its master; CH2 25KL / CH3 100KL either in the power-amp feedback (relay energised) or as a treble shunt on the stack output; ganged

controls.label: Mode
controls.note: Clean = CH1 (green; RY1, RY1', RY2 and the V2a J175 in their CH1 state). Raw / Vintage / Modern = the high-gain channel chosen by hgch with its Raw/Vtg/Mdrn switch in that position: Raw energises RY6 (lifts the .002 // 680K), Modern energises RY7 (180 pF on the CH3 treble cap, global feedback open), Vintage/Modern energise RY9 on CH3; RY8 is energised whenever CH2 is selected (decoded from the voicing sheet RECBSW2.501, see notes)

controls.label: Channel
controls.note: Which high-gain channel the Raw/Vintage/Modern modes use (RY3, RY4, RY8/RY9). The catalogue has one mode selector; CH3 (red) is the default

controls.label: CH1 Cln/Pushed
controls.note: CH1 Cln/Pushed switch (607101): RY5 / RY5'

controls.label: Rectifier
controls.note: Rear RECTIFIER SELECT (602112): silicon 1N4007 strings switched in parallel with the two 5U4s

controls.label: Bold/Spongy
controls.note: Rear BOLD/SPONGY switch (600115): primary tap; Spongy scales every secondary by 0.9 (assumption, see notes)

controls.label: FX Loop
controls.note: RY10 (FX LOOP BYPASS): Active runs V4a / Send / Mix / V4b / Output / Solo with nothing patched; Bypass goes from the master bus straight to the PI

controls.label: Solo
controls.note: Footswitch / EXT SOLO: On lifts the J175 across the SOLO pot

controls.label: Output
controls.note: Front-panel OUTPUT 250KA (loop active only); no catalogue param

controls.label: Solo Level
controls.note: Front-panel SOLO 250KA; heard with Solo on

controls.label: Send Level
controls.note: Rear SEND LEVEL 25KA; also sets the dry level into V4b

controls.label: Mix
controls.note: Rear MIX 25KL, 0 = dry (send wiper). With the return unpatched the bottom end is open

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Stored only

controls.label: VAC
controls.note: Stored only: the real line-voltage switch is Bold/Spongy (the power face switch), which uses the source scale

controls.label: Sag
controls.note: Sag emerges from the 5U4/silicon supply and choke; stored only

controls.label: Response
controls.note: No counterpart; stored only

controls.label: Bias
controls.note: The amp's bias is fixed (rear BIAS SELECT 6L6/EL34, left in the 6L6 position for the fitted 6L6s); stored only

controls.label: Power
controls.note: Catalogue 'Power' (id Hz), continuous and unused by the legacy model; the drawing has no continuous power control (no 50/100 W switch on this head). Bold/Spongy is the power face switch. Stored only

controls.label: On/Off
controls.note: Host handles bypass

multirate.note: Event-local oversampling (docs §10.48, §10.63): base 96 kHz, 8 substeps (768 kHz) on every LTE event of the signal group. The 3130 Hz gate tone folded about the 96 kHz base at -39.4 / -34.6 / -34.9 dB (0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 FS, own-mains mask), now -86.5 / -82.0 / -74.5 (2900 Hz -68.7 / -62.0 / -56.2 -> -89.5 / -91.0 / -79.5). A 192 kHz base alone fails at 1.0 FS (-55.6); LTE tol 8 is cheaper (+28 %) but doubles the dimed SPICE-gate error (1.14 -> 2.21 %); a 192 kHz base with 4 substeps is closer to truth (0.023 / 0.059 %) for +59 %. Engine T/16 truth, audio band, lead / rock DI: 0.167 / 0.368 -> 0.065 / 0.125 %. 9900X real / driven: 42.8 / 46.7 -> 61.2 / 64.9 % of a core.
